one_liner: Header-only C++20 lock-free atomic weak/shared pointers, beating a commercial atomic<weak_ptr> implementation under contention.
what_it_does: Provides reference-counted smart-pointer types for building lock-free concurrent data structures in C++, including data structures with cyclic or back-pointer references. It is not a literal std::shared_ptr/weak_ptr/atomic<shared_ptr> substitute: it introduces its own type family (rc_ptr, atomic_rc_ptr, snapshot_ptr, weak_ptr, atomic_weak_ptr, weak_snapshot_ptr) modeled closely on the standard interface, plus a snapshot_ptr type with no stdlib equivalent for cheap thread-local reads.
how_it_is_fast: Uses 'concurrent deferred reference counting': reference-count updates are decoupled from object reclamation, which is handed to a pluggable safe-memory-reclamation backend (hazard pointers by default, or epoch-based/interval-based/Hyaline reclamation) bounding per-operation reclamation overhead. The snapshot_ptr/weak_snapshot_ptr types read the current object without incrementing the shared reference count, cutting atomic RMW traffic on hot traversal paths versus always producing a fully counted handle.
when_to_use: Lock-free concurrent data structures (queues, stacks, structures with back-pointers) that need atomic weak pointers, at medium-to-high thread counts where the paper shows the advantage growing (4.2x at P=8, 10x at P=192 on a 72-core/4-socket box)
You are currently bottlenecked on a commercial or hand-rolled atomic<weak_ptr>-style implementation (e.g. just::thread) under contention
You can target a C++20-concepts-capable compiler (GCC 9+, Clang 13+, AppleClang, or MSVC 19, all green in CI) and restructure pointer usage around cdrc's own types
You want to tune the throughput/memory tradeoff by swapping reclamation backends (hazard pointers vs EBR vs IBR vs Hyaline) for the same pointer API
A research or experimental system where vendoring a small, unmaintained, MIT header-only library is acceptable
when_not_to_use: You need a true drop-in replacement for std::shared_ptr/std::weak_ptr/std::atomic<weak_ptr> with no code changes — cdrc's types are similarly shaped but distinct and require rewriting the pointer hierarchy

Single-threaded or low-contention (P=1) hot paths: the paper's own data has CDRC 4.5x slower than a hand-tuned manual-reclamation queue at P=1, and non-default backends add explicit per-scope guard overhead
Memory-constrained environments — EBR and Hyaline backends trade higher memory for throughput, and the library documents higher memory use than manual reclamation when oversubscribed

You need dynamic_cast on managed pointers or easy debuggability of the managed object's storage — issue #6 (dynamic cast) is open, and issues #3/#4 flag the type-erased char-array storage as hard to inspect
You need active upstream support — no commits since 2022-07-03, 5 open issues, 2 open unmerged PRs

integration.dependencies: none for the library itself; benchmarks additionally need CMake 3.5+, Boost (program_options), hwloc, jemalloc, Python3+Matplotlib, and optionally Folly or just::thread
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (uses concepts); CI builds and tests pass on GCC 9, GCC 11, Clang 13, AppleClang, and MSVC 19
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows for the library (all three run in CI); benchmarks are Linux-only (require NUMA policy support)
integration.thread_safety: atomic_rc_ptr/atomic_weak_ptr are lock-free (is_always_lock_free() == true) and safe for concurrent load/store/CAS; rc_ptr/weak_ptr are safe to read/copy concurrently as long as no thread races a writer; snapshot_ptr/weak_snapshot_ptr are for single-thread-local use only and must not outlive the guard (for non-default backends) that created them
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: operation shapes (load/store/compare_and_swap/compare_exchange_weak) match std::atomic<weak_ptr>-style APIs like just::thread's, but adopting it means switching the whole pointer hierarchy to cdrc::rc_ptr/atomic_rc_ptr/weak_ptr, and non-default reclamation backends require wrapping accesses in explicit guard objects

gotchas: Default backend is hazard pointers (moderate throughput, low memory); switching to EBR or Hyaline for higher throughput requires wrapping every potentially concurrent access in an epoch_guard/hyaline_guard, and holding a guard too long delays reclamation
atomic_rc_ptr and atomic_weak_ptr have deleted copy and move constructors/assignment — they must be used in place (e.g. as class members), not stored by value in containers
Internal counted-object storage is a raw char array (type-erased); two long-open issues (#3 'getValue' typo, #4 debuggability) flag this as awkward to inspect in a debugger
dynamic_cast on managed pointers is not supported and is an open, unresolved request (issue #6) as of the last commit
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The only same-category sibling that is actually concurrency-focused is observable_unique_ptr/observer_ptr (oup), which targets single-threaded non-owning observers, not atomic weak pointers. Pick CDRC over oup when you need thread-safe, lock-free atomic<weak_ptr>-style pointers for lock-free concurrent data structures; pick oup instead for single-threaded ownership/observer tracking where a full shared_ptr/weak_ptr pair is overkill.
verified_claims_summary: PLDI '22 paper Sec. 5.2/Fig. 12: on a 4-socket 72-core machine (4x Xeon E7-8867 v4, GCC 9.2.1 -O3), in a lock-free doubly-linked queue benchmark using atomic weak back-pointers (pop-then-reinsert, P=1-192 threads), CDRC's atomic_weak_ptr beat just::thread's atomic<weak_ptr> by 4.2x at P=8 and 10x at P=192, with CDRC's margin over just::thread at P=1 around 15x (derived, not the paper's often-cited 67x figure, which is the hand-tuned manual-reclamation baseline vs just::thread). CDRC itself trails that manual-reclamation queue by 4.5x at P=1, 19% at P=8, and 33% at P=192.
status_note: Abandoned: no commits since 2022-07-03 despite a later recorded repo push (no new commits found); MIT-licensed, small and header-only enough to vendor, and CI still builds/tests green on GCC 9/11, Clang 13, AppleClang, and MSVC 19, but 5 issues and 2 PRs have sat open since 2022.
